```{r opts, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

Every figure the app makes, you can make in a few lines of R, and vice versa.

# Set up

```{r project-setup, eval=FALSE}
library(PlotTrellis)
proj <- pt_project(project_dir = "your-folder",
                   samples_txt = pt_example())
pt_tracks(proj)    # the tracks it has
pt_samples(proj)   # the samples it has
```

For your own data, give your `samples.txt` path instead of `pt_example()`.

# Choosing tracks and samples

Tracks are drawn top to bottom, in the order given.

```{r choosing, eval=FALSE}
# every track for every sample, in samples.txt order
fig <- pt_figure(proj, "Eya2", tracks = c("ATAC", "genes"))
pt_save(fig, "Eya2.pdf")   # or .svg, .png
```

Other alterations include:

```{r choosing-more, eval=FALSE}
# one sample
pt_figure(proj, "Eya2", tracks = c("ATAC", "genes"), samples = "LP")

# a sample per track (NA for a track without samples)
pt_figure(proj, "Eya2", tracks = c("HIC", "genes", "HIC", "genes"),
          samples = c("LP", NA, "Basal", NA))

# LP compared against Basal; the second is the reference
pt_figure(proj, "Eya2", tracks = c("ATAC", "ATAC_diff", "genes"),
          comparison = c("LP", "Basal"))

# grouped by sample instead of by track
pt_figure(proj, "Eya2", tracks = c("ATAC", "H3K36me3", "genes"),
          order = "sample")

# any coordinates instead of a gene
pt_figure(proj, region = "chr2:165,430,000-165,620,000",
          tracks = c("ATAC", "genes"))
```

Numbers work instead of names (`tracks = c(6, 1), samples = 2`), according to the order in
`samples.txt` visible through `pt_tracks(proj)` and `pt_samples(proj)`.

# Many genes

One file per gene:

```{r one-per-gene, eval=FALSE}
# gene symbols, or Ensembl gene IDs with or without version
de_genes <- c("Eya2", "Acot7", "Cxcl14")
for (gene in de_genes) {
  fig <- pt_figure(proj, gene, tracks = c("ATAC", "genes"),
                   title = gene)
  pt_save(fig, paste0(gene, ".pdf"))
}
```

All in one file, with `pt_stitch()`:

```{r stitch, eval=FALSE}
# gene symbols, or Ensembl gene IDs with or without version
de_genes <- c("Eya2", "Acot7", "Cxcl14")
figs <- list()
for (gene in de_genes)
  figs[[gene]] <- pt_figure(proj, gene, tracks = c("ATAC", "genes"),
                            title = gene)
pt_stitch(figs, "all_genes.pdf")                 # stacked
pt_stitch(figs, "all_genes_2col.pdf", ncol = 2)  # two columns
```

Note: `.pdf` and `.svg` stay vector files, with components and text 
you can edit in vector graphics editors (e.g. Illustrator)

# With other tools

`pt_grob()` turns a figure into a grid grob, making it compatible with patchwork, cowplot, gridExtra or beside your own ggplot (e.g. a PCA, a volcano plot).

Adding a separate plot with patchwork:

```{r grob, eval=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
g <- pt_grob(figs[["Eya2"]])
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()   # your plot
both <- wrap_elements(g) + p + plot_layout(widths = c(g$width, 4))
ggsave("Eya2_and_plot.pdf", both, width = g$width + 4 + 0.5,
       height = g$height + 0.5)
```

# Beyond the API

- **`pt_script(fig, "Eya2.R")`** writes a standalone R script that redraws the figure with
  plotgardener, for edits the API doesn't offer:
    - Tracks, their order, colours, heights, the region and settings: the **Edit here** block
      at the top.
    - Specific changes to visuals of tracks: each track type is drawn by its own `render_<type>()` function further
      down (e.g. `render_bw()` for coverage). Edit that one.
- **`run_plottrellis(proj)`** opens the same project in the app.

<script>
if (navigator.clipboard) document.querySelectorAll("pre").forEach(function (pre) {
  var button = document.createElement("button");
  button.className = "copy-code";
  button.textContent = "Copy";
  var code = pre.querySelector("code") || pre;
  var box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "code-box";
  pre.parentNode.insertBefore(box, pre);
  box.appendChild(pre);
  button.onclick = function () {
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(code.innerText).then(function () {
      button.textContent = "Copied";
      setTimeout(function () { button.textContent = "Copy"; }, 1500);
    });
  };
  box.appendChild(button);
});
</script>
